preference_rationale: We do not actually have ground truth labels here, so it is hard to set up an experiment like B's. Identification in this setting is judgement-based matching of data observations against real-world knowledge - less statistical in nature - and A is better suited to it. It should also not require any survey work: the institutions are prominent enough that an independent research subagent should unearth identifying geographic and demographic properties that are visible in our data, and A should be able to get to an individual bank name for at least some of the clusters. Neither plan is very good, which is why the call is weak.
why_loser_was_defensible: B narrows to an individual ticker, which is ultimately what the desk needs, and it is the only one of the two that attaches a calibrated confidence to a name. An analyst who weighted that above the cost of assembling ground truth would have taken B.
